rows.change: /reload enables tools newly added to defaultTools; restored but unregistered tools stay pending.
rows.notes: Reload and late registration keep tools pending. Owner decision (2026-10-08): follow upstream v1.1.0 on open and tree navigation: unbound transcript tools become pending and activate on registration; tools disabled or excluded stay off. As upstream, CLI sessions opened with an initial selection (flags, settings or MCP) apply that selection instead of restoring the transcript. The restored loadout is recorded at open or navigation (upstream records at the next prompt), because PiSharp resolves every later turn from the transcript. Also as upstream: a recorded tool whose declaration changed is restored by name with its current binding (on transcript restore, tree navigation and opens with initial names), a now-hidden recorded tool is skipped and stays pending, and navigating to a branch with no system message keeps the current tools. Owner decision (2026-10-08): as upstream, unknown or capped-out names in --tools, defaultTools, SDK initial names and explicit activation select nothing and never become pending; a --tools allowlisted MCP tool activates when it registers. A transcript or explicit system message with an unbound declaration stays strict. Deviations: upstream also activates codemode and deferred tools named in initial names (no codemode or tool_search yet); a background MCP publication does not re-activate an allowlisted tool the user has since turned off.

rows.change: codemode-deferred aliases codemode; server description; mcp_servers prompt section appended on change; background connection; .pi/mcp.json project overrides (1.0.1).
rows.notes: Implemented: codemode-deferred alias, description, .pi/mcp.json override rules, mcp_servers section through the existing append-on-change sections, background connection for non-direct servers, production sessions load <agent dir>/mcp.json and honour --no-mcp. Remaining: servers needing codemode or tool_search cannot connect in production until those ship (1.1.0.x); late tools publish at the next idle point; no 10 s cap on direct servers; background servers have no resource tools; project .pi/mcp.json is unread (no project-trust store); a session closing during a background catalog publication can still fault (core session race).

rows.change: authServerMetadataUrl, RFC 9207 iss, step-up scope union, credentials per server name + URL with migration, cimd registration, clientName, auth.provider bearer, cancellable sign-in, 15 s request timeouts.
rows.notes: Plus: mcp login/logout/add/remove/list CLI with upstream texts, --timeout over the whole sign-in, default client_name, durable mcp-auth.json backend with the shared lock file, production OAuth servers use stored tokens. Remaining: auth.provider servers are not connected in production; no per-server refresh lock; !command client secrets refused; login has no connect-first check or tool count.
